This letter is the Attorney General's order on your petition for disclosure of records
under the Oregon Public Records Law, ORS 192.410 to 192.505.11 Your petition, which
we received on October 19, 1994, asks the Attorney General to direct the Department of
Justice, Charitable Activities Section, to make available the identity of a complainant who
filed a complaint related to Eitel Belau, including an unredacted letter of August 3, 1994,
which purportedly discloses the identity of the complainant.11 For the reasons that follow,
we respectfully deny your petition.
The Public Records Law confers a right to inspect any public records of a public
body in Oregon, subject to certain exemptions and limitations. ~ ORS 192.420. If a
public record contains exempt and nonexempt material, the public body must separate the
materials and make the nonexempt material available for examination if it is "reasonably
possible" to do so while preserving the confidentiality of the exempt material. Turner v.
Reed, 22 Or App 177, 186 n 8, 538 P2d 373 (1975).
11 Your petition was filed on behalf of your client, Lily Ulitech, President, Eitel Belau
Corporation, who made the original public records request.
21 This agency has previously provided your client with a redacted copy of the August 3
letter.

1. Confidential Submission Exemption
ORS 192.502(3) exempts information submitted in confidence from the disclosure
requirements of the Public Records Law. This provision exempts from disclosure:
"Information submitted to a public body in confidence and not
otherwise required by law to be submitted, where such information should
reasonably be considered confidential, the public body has obliged itself in
good faith not to disclose the information and when the public interest would
suffer by the disclosure[.]"
The agency must be able to present evidence that there was a condition or
understanding at the time the information was provided that the information would be held in
confidence. Sadler v. Oregon State Bar, 275 Or 279, 550 P2d 1218 (1976). This exemption
clearly does not apply if the public agency requests that information be submitted in
confidence to avoid embarrassment to itself.
2. Discussion
A review of the Charitable Activity Section's Eitel Belau investigative file shows that
the complainant initially approached the agency with a written request for confidentiality.
This request for confidentiality was repeated in at least one subsequent letter providing
additional information to the agency's investigator. The agency investigator, Kirk Harvey,
wrote at least one memo to the file reciting the complainant's expectation of confidentiality.
Mr. Harvey's closing letter of August 3, 1994, confirmed, • ... we will make every attempt
to keep your identity confidential. • Mr. Harvey advises that this written statement confirms
his oral understanding with the complainant and that he had regularly communicated this
understanding to the complainant beginning from the inception of his contact with the
complainant.
In this instance, we conclude that the complainant submitted information, based on an
understanding of confidentiality. The agency's representative obligated the agency in good
faith not to disclose the complainant's identity. The information was submitted voluntarily,
and the complainant was under no legal obligation to come forward.
We also conclude that disclosure would cause harm to the public interest. The
purpose of this exemption is to encourage citizens to provide relevant information voluntarily
to governmental agencies with some reasonable assurance that the information will be kept
confidential. It is reasonable to conclude that this purpose would be defeated and this •
complainant and others would be deterred from coming forward if this pledge of

confidentiality was breached. We believe that this public policy is not overcome by mere
speculation that identification of the complainant might help identify the author of an
anonymous, but allegedly, defamatory letter circulated after the agency's investigation was
completed.
Because we find that the record you seek is exempt from disclosure under
ORS 192.502(3), we deny your petition.
